about: The sheet for the Pump House cutaway (working draft): tools/cutaway/sheet.py. Callouts are anchored to drawn parts (history ids, in the isometric view and the two flat sections); a badge's style is the anchored part's confidence unless `confidence` says otherwise. Callout text is a working draft, written with Claude, for the artist to edit.
title: The New Pump-House, Richmond, about 1885
subtitle: Canal water turns three wheels; the wheels drive nine pumps; people dance overhead
sectionCaption: Cut along the machine room, looking north

crossSection.caption: Cut across through the middle wheel, looking west: the forebay on the right

callouts.title: The forebay
callouts.text: The Pump House Canal, dammed at the east end. Its water stood level with the walkway along the north front.

callouts.title: Sluice gates
callouts.text: A gate 6 ft square at the head of each penstock, worked by a hydraulic cylinder on the wall’s top.

callouts.title: Penstocks
callouts.text: Iron pipes 5 ft across falling from the gates under a 20-ft head, each turned into the center of its wheel.

callouts.title: Three turbine wheels
callouts.text: Partial outward-flow wheels of the Fourneyron type, all iron, 23 ft across, struck from the center.

callouts.title: Diffuser
callouts.text: A cast-iron diffuser under each wheel eased the spent water into the tailrace.

callouts.title: Tailraces
callouts.text: Vaulted tunnels under the south walkway carried the water out to the canal below the locks.

callouts.title: The canal below the locks
callouts.text: The canal’s lower level, 20 ft below the forebay. The water went on to the mills downtown.

callouts.title: Shafts, cranks and rods
callouts.text: Each wheel turned a 12-in shaft with three cranks set 120° apart. Rods 16 ft long worked crossheads in guides overhead.

callouts.title: Nine plunger pumps
callouts.text: Three to a wheel, 14-in plungers with a 6-ft stroke: 12 million gallons a day in all.

callouts.title: Lattice girders
callouts.text: Iron girders across the room carried the crosshead guides under the dance floor.

callouts.title: The mains
callouts.text: A 36-in suction from the forebay; a 30-in main 3,600 ft up to the New Reservoir, 175 ft higher.

callouts.title: The pavilion
callouts.text: An open-air dance floor over the machines. It was the machine room’s only roof, and rain came through: glazed in 1899.

callouts.title: The arcade
callouts.text: Six Tudor arches each side on seven cast-iron columns, with railings of zinc-coated tin.

callouts.title: The wings
callouts.text: Granite, with slate roofs and lancet windows; stairs at the south corners, powder rooms and offices upstairs.

key: drawn from a plan, a section or a survey
marksNote: The same marks stand by each part in the two sections.
travelerKey: Visitors to scale, 1.75 m (5 ft 9 in) tall, for size only: no source says who came. The red line is the water’s way.
sources: Sources: The American Engineer, Dec. 26, 1884, pp. 260–261 (HathiTrust); National Register nomination, New Pump-House, 2002; HAER VA-34 (Library of Congress); Pump House Park schematic design study, 2019 (levels); C. E. Bolling, AWWA Proceedings, 1900; OpenStreetMap; USGS 3DEP.
notes: The machines are scaled from the 1884 engravings by the dimensions in their text. Where each gang stood, the tailraces and the roof’s pitch are inferred. The roof is lifted off and the middle of the floor taken up. The canals’ banks are today’s.
